11	Cumulative rules as of Sprint 3 (2026-11). Graded per PR out of 20: implements ACs 6 · tests + Test Evidence 6 · what/why + Tech Debt + linked issue 3 · CI or manual verification 3 · rubric review + approval on latest commit 2.
12	
13	**Why:** these are graded line by line, and missing sections cost points even when the code is right.
14	**How to apply:** run through this list whenever drafting a branch, commit, PR body, or review.
15	
16	## Branch & commit
17	
18	- One branch per issue, cut from an up-to-date `master` (the course site says `main`; this repo uses `master`). Names: `feat/issue-<n>-<slug>`, `fix/issue-<n>-<slug>`.
19	- Commit: conventional prefix + issue number, e.g. `feat: add PDF export for reports (#42)`. The repo's agent rules also require an `[AI]` prefix on commits and PR titles made by an agent, so `[AI] feat: … (#42)`.
20	- Never push to `master` (it's protected). After merging, switch to `master`, pull, and delete the branch locally and on GitHub.
21	
22	## PR body (all required)
23	
24	1. `Closes #<issue>` (course wording; upstream uses `Fixes #` — `Closes` is fine). Attach the PR to the `Sprint N` milestone.
25	2. **What changed and why**, in the student's own words.
26	3. **Tech Debt** section with both fields: **Introduced:** (shortcuts or compromises made here, and why) and **Encountered:** (pre-existing debt met, and how it was handled). Write "None." when there is none.
27	4. **Test Evidence** section (S3+, replaces "how it was tested"):
28	   | Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
29	   - One row per AC from the issue (for bugs, use the Expected Behavior instead). If there's no product behavior change (CI-only, etc.), write N/A and explain.
30	   - Test(s): test name + file; manual checks are written `Manual: <steps> → <result>`; list both if an AC is covered both ways.
31	   - Level: `unit` / `integration` / `E2E` / `manual`.
32	   - Source: `AC` / `issue discussion` / `docs` / `upstream behavior` / `other (explain)`. **The current output of our own code is never a valid source.**
33	   - Plus: **Not tested automatically, and why** (manual rows only), and **AI-written tests**: list tests AI wrote or changed and how their expected values were verified ("None" if none).
34	5. CI result. If CI isn't running, list the commands run and their pass/fail/skip counts (`yarn typecheck`, `yarn lint`, the workspace test command).
35	6. New or updated tests for every behavior change.
36	
37	- Upstream Definition of Done (docs/sprint0/standards.md) also expects `yarn typecheck`, `yarn lint:fix`, and passing tests to be run, plus a release note in `upcoming-release-notes/` (use the writing-release-notes skill).
38	- **Conflict to raise with the user:** `.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md` says agents should leave the PR template unfilled, but the course grades the PR body. Draft the course sections for the user and ask how they want them placed, rather than silently following either rule.
39	
40	## Review & merge
41	
42	- No self-approval or self-merge. At least one teammate approves; **merge only if that approval is on the latest commit** (any push after approval needs a new approval).
43	- Request the review on GitHub and ping the reviewer on Zulip. Reviewers reply within 24h.
44	- The reviewer posts a **rubric comment during the first review pass**, before the author revises, scoring 1–10 with a 1–2 sentence note each: Correctness · Test coverage · Code quality · Documentation · AI transparency (evidence of human verification) · **Test evidence** (S3: does every AC have a test, are expected values justified, which tests did the reviewer run locally) · Overall (merge as-is?). "LGTM" or approval alone doesn't count.
45	- Everyone reviews at least once per sprint, and everyone must review every teammate at least once over the semester.
46	- Anything posted to GitHub by the agent starts with 🤖 (repo rule).
47	- The student must be able to explain every line. When implementing, explain the changes, rationale, and risks before they're accepted.
48	- Skipped tests and disabled checks need a linked issue and a reason in a code comment. The team may not introduce new test failures.
49

+import type { RuleEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
+
+import { duplicateRule } from '#util/rule';
+
+const rule: RuleEntity = {
+  id: 'rule-1',
+  stage: 'pre',
+  conditionsOp: 'or',
+  conditions: [{ field: 'payee', op: 'is', value: 'payee-1', type: 'id' }],
+  actions: [{ op: 'set', field: 'category', value: 'cat-1', type: 'id' }],
+};
+
+describe('duplicateRule', () => {
+  it('copies the rule options without its id', () => {
+    const copy = duplicateRule(rule);
+
+    expect(copy).not.toHaveProperty('id');
+    expect(copy).toEqual({
+      stage: 'pre',
+      conditionsOp: 'or',
+      conditions: rule.conditions,
+      actions: rule.actions,
+    });
+  });
+
+  it('does not share conditions or actions with the original', () => {
+    const copy = duplicateRule(rule);
+
+    expect(copy.conditions).not.toBe(rule.conditions);
+    expect(copy.conditions[0]).not.toBe(rule.conditions[0]);
+    expect(copy.actions).not.toBe(rule.actions);
+    expect(copy.actions[0]).not.toBe(rule.actions[0]);
+  });
+
+  it('drops the schedule link but keeps the other actions', () => {
+    const copy = duplicateRule({
+      ...rule,
+      actions: [
+        { op: 'link-schedule', value: 'schedule-1' },
+        { op: 'set', field: 'notes', value: 'rent', type: 'string' },
+      ],
+    });
+
+    expect(copy.conditions).toEqual(rule.conditions);
+    expect(copy.actions).toEqual([
+      { op: 'set', field: 'notes', value: 'rent', type: 'string' },
+    ]);
+  });
+
+  it('adds a blank category action when the schedule link was the only action', () => {
+    const copy = duplicateRule({
+      ...rule,
+      actions: [{ op: 'link-schedule', value: 'schedule-1' }],
+    });
+
+    expect(copy.actions).toEqual([
+      { op: 'set', field: 'category', value: null, type: 'id' },
+    ]);
+  });
+});

+export function duplicateRule(rule: RuleEntity): NewRuleEntity {
+  // A schedule owns exactly one rule; saving a second rule that links to it
+  // would re-point the schedule at the copy. Drop the link so the copy is a
+  // standalone rule.
+  const actions = structuredClone(rule.actions).filter(
+    action => action.op !== 'link-schedule',
+  );
+
+  return {
+    stage: rule.stage,
+    conditionsOp: rule.conditionsOp,
+    conditions: structuredClone(rule.conditions),
+    actions:
+      actions.length > 0
+        ? actions
+        : [{ op: 'set', field: 'category', value: null, type: 'id' }],
+  };
+}

<!-- Thank you for submitting a pull request! Make sure to follow the instructions to write release notes for your PR — it should only take a minute or two: https://actualbudget.org/docs/contributing/#writing-good-release-notes. Try running yarn generate:release-notes *before* pushing your PR for an interactive experience. -->

## Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Why is it needed? Please give context on the "why?": why do we need this change? What problem is it solving for you?-->

Adds a **Duplicate** button to the Rules page. Until now, every new rule had to be built from scratch, even when it was almost the same as an existing one. Duplicate opens the rule editor already filled in with a copy of the selected rule. The user can change what they need and save it as a new rule, and the original rule is not changed.

Changes:

- **Duplicate button:** `ManageRules.tsx`. The button is always shown at the bottom right, next to "Create new rule". It is enabled only when exactly one rule is selected. When it's disabled, a tooltip says why: "Select a rule to duplicate" or "Select only one rule to duplicate".
- **Copying a rule:** `duplicateRule()` in `util/rule.ts`. It makes a full copy of the rule's stage, conditions and actions without the rule's `id`. Because there is no `id`, the editor saves the copy through `rule-add` as a new rule instead of updating the original with `rule-update` (`RuleEditor.tsx`, `onSave`).
- **Rules linked to schedules:** these can be duplicated too, but the copy does not keep the "link schedule" action. Saving a rule that links to a schedule points that schedule at the saved rule (`onRuleUpdate` in `loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts`), so a copy that kept the link would quietly take the schedule over from the original rule. The copy keeps all of the conditions. If the schedule link was its only action, it gets a blank "set category" action, the same one "Create new rule" starts with.
- **Tests:** 4 unit tests in `util/rule.test.ts` and 2 e2e tests in `e2e/rules.test.ts`. The `RulesPage` page model gets `selectNthRule()` and `duplicateSelectedRule()`.
- **Release note:** `upcoming-release-notes/duplicate-rules.md`.

No screenshots are added or changed. With no rule selected, the Rules page only gains a disabled button in the footer.

<!-- If AI tools wrote a significant part of this change, please disclose it here and name the tool you used. See https://actualbudget.org/docs/contributing/ai-usage-policy -->

**AI disclosure:** the feature code, tests, page-model helpers and release note were written with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5).

## Related issue(s)

<!-- e.g. Fixes #123, Relates to #456 -->

Closes #159

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: A "Duplicate" button appears in the bottom right when a rule is selected | `duplicates a rule without changing the original` | e2e | The issue says the button should be usable only with one rule selected. The test checks it is disabled with no rule selected, disabled with two selected, and enabled with one. With 0 or 2 selected, the tooltip text must match the strings in `ManageRules.tsx` |
| AC2: The rule window opens pre-filled and can be edited | `duplicates a rule without changing the original`; unit test `copies the rule options without its id` | e2e + unit | The editor's first condition must contain `Fast Internet`, the payee of the rule being copied. The test then changes the category to `Food`. In the unit test, the copy must have the same stage, conditions and actions as the original, and no `id` |
| AC3: The new rule is saved and the original is not changed | `duplicates a rule without changing the original`; unit test `does not share conditions or actions with the original` | e2e + unit | After saving, both `set category to General` (the original) and `set category to Food` (the copy) are listed. The unit test checks that the copy's conditions and actions are new objects, so editing the copy can't change the original |
| AC3 (schedule rules): duplicating a schedule rule leaves the original linked to its schedule | `duplicates a schedule rule without taking over the schedule`; unit tests `drops the schedule link but keeps the other actions` and `adds a blank category action when the schedule link was the only action` | e2e + unit | The demo budget has exactly one rule for "Fast Internet", and it links to a schedule. After duplicating it, the list shows the original's `link schedule …` action plus `set category to Food` for the copy. Why the link is dropped: `onRuleUpdate` in `schedules/app.ts` |
| AC4: The new rule is still there between sessions | `duplicates a rule without changing the original` (after `page.reload()`) | e2e | After a reload, the budget is read again from its local database, and both rules must still be listed with their categories |
| No regressions: typecheck and lint pass | All | Local / CI | `yarn typecheck`, oxlint and oxfmt pass locally. The 4 unit tests and both new e2e tests pass in Chromium. CI result: All Pass |

**Not tested automatically, and why:**

- **Mobile Rules page:** the issue describes the desktop Rules window, and this PR does not add Duplicate on mobile.
- **How the tooltip and button look:** not covered by VRT. The e2e test checks the tooltip text and whether the button is enabled, not how they look. The existing Rules screenshots aren't affected, since they're taken with no rule selected and the button doesn't change the layout.
- **The other tests in `rules.test.ts`:** not run locally, because they compare screenshots that have to be generated in the Linux Docker image. CI covers them.
- **"Between sessions" means a page reload:** the test reloads the page instead of closing and reopening the app. Both read the budget from the same local database.

**AI-written tests:** Claude Code wrote all 6 tests and the page-model helpers. The expected values were checked like this:

- **Traced to source:** each expected value was compared with the source listed in the table above. For example, `onSave` in `RuleEditor.tsx` chooses `rule-add` when the rule has no `id`, and `onRuleUpdate` in `schedules/app.ts` explains why the copy can't keep the schedule link.
- **Run locally:** each test was run in Chromium, and the first e2e version failed for real reasons. The demo budget already has a schedule rule for "Fast Internet", so the row counts were wrong. The test also clicked a rule before the editor had finished closing. Both were fixed in the test; the feature code didn't need changes.

Add ability to duplicate rules
## Title
Add ability to duplicate rules

## Summary
When adding rules, you have to start from scratch each time. There are a number of different options to choose from in the dropdown menus, and it can be frustrating to remake rules that are the same or similar for multiple rules. When starting to use an app, People with very little patience would benefit from this feature.

## User Story
As a very lazy person, I want to be able to duplicate rules so that I spend less time setting up my budgeting app.

## User Scenario
When creating rules, the user would have the option to select a pre-existing rule and click a button in the bottom right corner the says "Duplicate." This would then bring up the Rule window with each option pre-filled in with the pre-existing rule's options. Then, the user could edit the rule as needed and save it.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A button appears in the bottom right-hand corner when selecting a rule that says "Duplicate."
2. The Rule window appears and allows the user to edit the options.
3. The new rule is saved, as well as the pre-existing rule not having been edited.
4. The new rule exists between sessions with the options set.

## Rough Scope
Medium (4) - it requires a UI change as well as understanding how rules are created and saved in the code base.

## Out of Scope
- Editing multiple rules at once
- Adding new options for rules

## Open Questions
- Design decisions?
- How would one ensure that the option is only available when one rule is selected?
- How are rules created and saved in the code base?

## Source
- My own exploring

I ran every check against PR 181 and they all pass. Besides the two problems you spotted, I found one wrong explanation in the code and several gaps in the PR description.

| Check | Result |

| GitHub CI on the latest commit | Everything passes, including the visual regression and e2e checks |

I didn't run the screenshot tests locally, because they have to be generated in the Linux Docker image and there's no Docker here. CI's visual regression check passes on the updated screenshots.

## Code review

The change is small and works. Duplicating opens the editor with a copy that has no `id`, so `RuleEditor`'s save creates a new rule instead of updating the original. The copy gets its own conditions and actions, so editing it can't change the original rule. Findings for the author:

1. **Wrong reason in the code comment** ([rule.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/util/rule.ts)) and repeated in the PR description. It says a copy that kept the schedule link "would re-point the schedule at the copy." It wouldn't: saving a rule with that link never changes which rule a schedule uses. What happens instead (`onRuleUpdate` in `loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts`) is that the schedule's saved condition positions (`schedules_json_paths`) get overwritten with the copy's. Those positions say where the schedule's date, amount and payee are in its rule, so the original schedule can show wrong data once the copy is edited. The copy would also link matching transactions to the schedule. Dropping the link is still right; only the explanation needs fixing.
2. **AC1 differs from the issue.** The issue says the button "appears when selecting a rule". The PR always shows it, disabled, with a tooltip saying why. That's a reasonable choice, but the PR should say it was deliberate.
3. **Small edge case:** the "Select only one rule" tooltip would also show if exactly one rule is selected but can't be found in the rule list. That's very unlikely, so it isn't worth blocking on.

## PR description and course requirements

- **Two release notes** (as you saw). `feat-duplicate-rules.md` was added in the later "Add release notes" commit and the description only names `duplicate-rules.md`, so the first one should be deleted.
- **Missing AI log** (confirmed). There's no `ai-logs/sprint3/RaccoonSwarm/` folder on master or on the PR branch, and no AI Assistance comment.
- **Screenshots contradict the description.** It says "No screenshots are added or changed" and that the existing Rules screenshots aren't affected. In fact VRT failed, and 6 screenshots were updated in `1032b9ac1`.
- **No Tech Debt section** (Introduced/Encountered), which the course requires.

  - The "No regressions" row isn't one of the issue's ACs.
- **"CI result: All Pass"** is true now, but it was written before the screenshot fix.

**Is hiding the button hard?** No, it's easy. In [ManageRules.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/ManageRules.tsx), the button would follow the same pattern as the existing "Delete N rules" button right above it:

```tsx
{canDuplicate && (
  <Button onPress={onDuplicateSelected}>
    <Trans>Duplicate</Trans>
  </Button>
)}
```

The `Tooltip` wrapper, its two strings and the `Tooltip` import all go away. The e2e test needs a small change too: check that the button isn't there with 0 or 2 rules selected, instead of checking that it's disabled and its tooltip text.

Hiding it also undoes the screenshot problem. The Rules screenshots are taken with no rule selected, so the footer would look exactly as it does on master. The screenshot commit `1032b9ac1` can then be reverted, which also makes "no screenshots changed" true again.

**Why did they skip it?** I can't tell for sure. The issue lists "How would one ensure that the option is only available when one rule is selected?" as an open question, and nothing on the issue answers it. The PR shows a deliberate "always visible, disabled, tooltip explains why" design, so it was probably a choice, not something they found too hard. That pattern helps people find the feature, so it's defensible, but it doesn't match AC1. If they want to keep it, they should say so in the PR and get the team to agree to change the AC.

+import type { RuleEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
+
+import { duplicateRule } from '#util/rule';
+
+const rule: RuleEntity = {
+  id: 'rule-1',
+  stage: 'pre',
+  conditionsOp: 'or',
+  conditions: [{ field: 'payee', op: 'is', value: 'payee-1', type: 'id' }],
+  actions: [{ op: 'set', field: 'category', value: 'cat-1', type: 'id' }],
+};
+
+describe('duplicateRule', () => {
+  it('copies the rule options without its id', () => {
+    const copy = duplicateRule(rule);
+
+    expect(copy).not.toHaveProperty('id');
+    expect(copy).toEqual({
+      stage: 'pre',
+      conditionsOp: 'or',
+      conditions: rule.conditions,
+      actions: rule.actions,
+    });
+  });
+
+  it('does not share conditions or actions with the original', () => {
+    const copy = duplicateRule(rule);
+
+    expect(copy.conditions).not.toBe(rule.conditions);
+    expect(copy.conditions[0]).not.toBe(rule.conditions[0]);
+    expect(copy.actions).not.toBe(rule.actions);
+    expect(copy.actions[0]).not.toBe(rule.actions[0]);
+  });
+
+  it('drops the schedule link but keeps the other actions', () => {
+    const copy = duplicateRule({
+      ...rule,
+      actions: [
+        { op: 'link-schedule', value: 'schedule-1' },
+        { op: 'set', field: 'notes', value: 'rent', type: 'string' },
+      ],
+    });
+
+    expect(copy.conditions).toEqual(rule.conditions);
+    expect(copy.actions).toEqual([
+      { op: 'set', field: 'notes', value: 'rent', type: 'string' },
+    ]);
+  });
+
+  it('adds a blank category action when the schedule link was the only action', () => {
+    const copy = duplicateRule({
+      ...rule,
+      actions: [{ op: 'link-schedule', value: 'schedule-1' }],
+    });
+
+    expect(copy.actions).toEqual([
+      { op: 'set', field: 'category', value: null, type: 'id' },
+    ]);
+  });
+});

 // @ts-strict-ignore

+import type { NewRuleEntity, RuleEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
 import { t } from 'i18next';

@@ -159,3 +159,23 @@ export function translateRuleStage(stage: string): string {

   }
 }
+
+export function duplicateRule(rule: RuleEntity): NewRuleEntity {
+  // Drop the schedule link so the copy is a standalone rule. A copy that kept
+  // it would overwrite the schedule's schedules_json_paths entry when saved
+  // (onRuleUpdate in schedules/app.ts) and link the transactions it matches
+  // to the schedule.
+  const actions = structuredClone(rule.actions).filter(
+    action => action.op !== 'link-schedule',
+  );
+
+  return {
+    stage: rule.stage,
+    conditionsOp: rule.conditionsOp,
+    conditions: structuredClone(rule.conditions),
+    actions:
+      actions.length > 0
+        ? actions
+        : [{ op: 'set', field: 'category', value: null, type: 'id' }],
+  };
+}

<!-- Thank you for submitting a pull request! Make sure to follow the instructions to write release notes for your PR — it should only take a minute or two: https://actualbudget.org/docs/contributing/#writing-good-release-notes. Try running yarn generate:release-notes *before* pushing your PR for an interactive experience. -->

## Description

Adds a **Duplicate** button to the Rules page. Until now, every new rule had to be built from scratch, even when it was almost the same as an existing one. Duplicate opens the rule editor already filled in with a copy of the selected rule. The user can change what they need and save it as a new rule, and the original rule is not changed.

Changes:

- **Duplicate button:** `ManageRules.tsx`. The button appears at the bottom right, next to "Create new rule", only when exactly one rule is selected. It works the same way as the existing "Delete N rules" button, which only appears when rules are selected.
- **Copying a rule:** `duplicateRule()` in `util/rule.ts`. It makes a full copy of the rule's stage, conditions and actions without the rule's `id`. Because there is no `id`, the editor saves the copy through `rule-add` as a new rule instead of updating the original with `rule-update` (`RuleEditor.tsx`, `onSave`).
- **Rules linked to schedules:** these can be duplicated too, but the copy does not keep the "link schedule" action. A copy that kept the link would do two things:
  - When saved, it would overwrite the schedule's `schedules_json_paths` entry with its own condition positions (`onRuleUpdate` in `loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts`, which uses `INSERT OR REPLACE` keyed by schedule id).
  - Whenever it ran, it would link the transactions it matches to the schedule (the `link-schedule` case in `loot-core/src/server/rules/action.ts` sets `transaction.schedule`).

  The copy keeps all of the conditions. If the schedule link was its only action, it gets a blank "set category" action, the same one "Create new rule" starts with.
- **Tests:** 4 unit tests in `util/rule.test.ts` and 2 e2e tests in `e2e/rules.test.ts`. The `RulesPage` page model gets `selectNthRule()` and `duplicateSelectedRule()`.
- **Release note:** `upcoming-release-notes/duplicate-rules.md`.

**Screenshots:** this PR changes no VRT screenshots. An earlier version of this PR always showed the button, disabled, which changed the Rules page footer, so 6 Rules screenshots were updated. Now the button is hidden unless one rule is selected. All Rules screenshots are taken with no rule selected, so they match master again, and those 6 screenshots have been restored to master's versions.

**AI disclosure:** the feature code, tests, page-model helpers and release note were written with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5). 

## Related issue(s)

Closes #159

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion (from #159) | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: A button appears in the bottom right-hand corner when selecting a rule that says "Duplicate." | `duplicates a rule without changing the original` | e2e | AC1 says the button *appears* when a rule is selected. The issue's open question asks how to make the option "only available when one rule is selected". So the test expects a button named exactly `Duplicate` to be hidden with no rule selected, visible with one rule selected, hidden again with two rules selected, and visible again when one of them is deselected. |
| AC2: The Rule window appears and allows the user to edit the options. | `duplicates a rule without changing the original`; unit test `copies the rule options without its id` | e2e + unit | The user scenario says the window opens "with each option pre-filled in with the pre-existing rule's options". In the e2e test, the editor's first condition must contain `Fast Internet`, the payee of the rule being copied, and the test then changes the category to `Food`. In the unit test, the copy must have the same stage, conditions and actions as the original, and no `id`. |
| AC3: The new rule is saved, as well as the pre-existing rule not having been edited. | `duplicates a rule without changing the original`; unit test `does not share conditions or actions with the original` | e2e + unit | After saving, both `set category to General` (the original, unchanged) and `set category to Food` (the copy) must be listed. The unit test checks that the copy's conditions and actions are new objects, so editing the copy can't change the original. |
| AC3 (schedule rules): the pre-existing rule is not edited, including its schedule link | `duplicates a schedule rule without taking over the schedule`; unit tests `drops the schedule link but keeps the other actions` and `adds a blank category action when the schedule link was the only action` | e2e + unit | The demo budget has exactly one rule for "Fast Internet", and it links to a schedule. After duplicating it, the list must show the original's `link schedule …` action plus `set category to Food` for the copy. The reason the copy drops the link is explained under "Rules linked to schedules" above. |
| AC4: The new rule exists between sessions with the options set. | `duplicates a rule without changing the original` (after `page.reload()`) | e2e | After a reload, the budget is read again from its local database, and both rules must still be listed with their categories. |

**Run locally** (after merging master into this branch):

- `yarn typecheck`: passes.
- oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files: pass.
- The 4 unit tests in `util/rule.test.ts`: pass.
- Both new e2e tests (`yarn playwright test e2e/rules.test.ts -g "duplicates"`): pass.

**Not tested automatically, and why:**

- **Mobile Rules page:** the issue describes the desktop Rules window, and this PR does not add Duplicate on mobile.
- **The screenshot tests in `rules.test.ts`:** not run locally, because the screenshots have to be generated in the Linux Docker image. CI covers them.
- **"Between sessions" means a page reload:** the test reloads the page instead of closing and reopening the app. Both read the budget from the same local database.

**AI-written tests:** Claude Code wrote all 6 tests and the page-model helpers. The expected values were checked like this:

- **Traced to source:** each expected value was compared with the issue text or the code listed in the table above. For example, `onSave` in `RuleEditor.tsx` chooses `rule-add` when the rule has no `id`, and `onRuleUpdate` in `schedules/app.ts` shows why the copy can't keep the schedule link.
- **Run locally:** each test was run, and the first e2e version failed for real reasons. The demo budget already has a schedule rule for "Fast Internet", so the row counts were wrong. The test also clicked a rule before the editor had finished closing. Both were fixed in the test; the feature code didn't need changes.
- **Manually tested:** I tried the feature on the demo budget on my machine.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**

- **The schedule link is dropped without telling the user.** When a schedule rule is duplicated, the editor opens without the "link schedule" action and doesn't say why. A short notice in the editor would make this clearer.
- **Duplicate is harder to discover.** Because the button only appears with exactly one rule selected, users won't see that duplicating exists until they select a rule. This matches the "Delete N rules" button and AC1.
- **No Duplicate on mobile.** Mobile users still have to build similar rules from scratch.

**Encountered:**

- **`ManageRules.tsx` and `util/rule.ts` both start with `// @ts-strict-ignore`**, so the new code in them, including `duplicateRule()`, isn't checked in TypeScript strict mode. `duplicateRule()` has explicit `RuleEntity` / `NewRuleEntity` types, and its unit tests cover its output, but strict mode would catch more. This PR doesn't change it, because making those whole files strict is outside its scope.
